Steady Output Marks Q2 for UK Metals & Mining Sector

The UK’s Metals & Mining industry reported stable trade figures in the second quarter of 2024, with output and exports broadly in line with the same period last year, according to data released Thursday by the British Mining Association (BMA). 

Total metal ore extraction stood at 5.2 million tonnes for the quarter, a marginal rise of 0.8% year-on-year. Refined metal exports reached 1.7 million tonnes, maintaining a similar pace to Q2 2023. Domestic demand for steel and non-ferrous metals remained robust, underpinned by continued investment in construction and automotive manufacturing.

“We’re seeing consistent performance across most segments, with no major disruptions or supply chain bottlenecks,” said John Cresswell, senior analyst at British Commodities Insights. “Producers have managed to maintain steady output levels, benefitting from stable energy costs and predictable order books.”

Leading operators such as Northvale Minerals and Wessex Metals reported output within anticipated ranges. The BMA noted that employment across the sector remains unchanged, with approximately 41,000 people employed directly in extraction and processing.

Market participants observed that global prices for aluminium and copper continued to fluctuate within their recent bands, but had little impact on UK export volumes. “We’re in a period of relative calm, which is always welcome for planning and investment,” said Maria Ellison, spokesperson for the National Miners’ Union.

Looking ahead, analysts expect sustained demand from infrastructure projects and a steady pipeline of export orders. “It’s a solid, uneventful quarter, and that’s often good news in this industry,” Cresswell added. The BMA will release its full mid-year report in July.
